algorithm.Title: Insect Bite - Male (Adult)
algorithm.ContentSet: IST Open-Source Guideline Content | Adult | Male
Definition: General insect bite assessment (unknown insect) decomposed from NHS.UK's published insect bites and stings guidance.
FirstAid: Call Qatar 999 now. Use the patient's prescribed adrenaline auto-injector immediately for suspected anaphylaxis and follow its plan. Do not allow standing, walking, or driving; position for breathing and consciousness and follow the call-handler. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.

questions.Question: Are throat or tongue swelling, breathing difficulty, faintness, confusion, or collapse the main concern?
questions.Information: Systemic allergic-reaction features require the Anaphylaxis pathway.

questions.Question: Is there swelling of the lips, mouth, throat or tongue, breathing difficulty, wheeze, collapse, reduced responsiveness, blue/grey colour, widespread hives with vomiting or dizziness, or a rapidly progressive reaction?
questions.Information: NHS.UK insect bites and stings guidance lists these as signs of a serious allergic reaction (anaphylaxis) requiring an immediate 999 call.

questions.Question: Without an emergency feature, are symptoms worsening, is the bite in the mouth, throat or near the eye, are there multiple bites, fever, abdominal pain, vomiting or dizziness, or is the patient an infant, pregnant, immunocompromised, or previously severely allergic?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance lists these as reasons to seek clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) or arrange clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED) urgently.

questions.Question: Is the skin around the bite hot, red, painful, swollen, or leaking pus or fluid (signs of infection)?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance flags these infection signs as needing a pharmacist or clinical review through a Qatar pathway approved by governance (GOVERNANCE_REQUIRED).

questions.Question: Is this a single, minor bite with none of the features above?
questions.Information: NHS.UK guidance describes minor bites without infection or allergy signs as manageable at home.

advice.Title: Emergency insect-reaction precautions
Content: Call Qatar 999 now. Use the patient's prescribed adrenaline auto-injector immediately for suspected anaphylaxis and follow its plan. Do not allow standing, walking, or driving; position for breathing and consciousness and follow the call-handler. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care.
Call Back If: breathing, swelling, vomiting, dizziness, collapse, or consciousness worsens.

advice.Title: Prompt in-person bite review
Content: Use the Qatar governance-approved in-person service. Remove a visible stinger by scraping if easy, wash the area, and use a wrapped cool pack. Do not squeeze venom sacs or use unverified remedies. Medication requires age, pregnancy and comorbidity checks.
Call Back If: swelling spreads, fever, vomiting, dizziness, severe pain, or breathing change.

advice.Title: Routine bite follow-up
Content: Keep the area clean and book a routine review for signs of infection.
Call Back If: increasing redness or pain; fever develops.

advice.Title: Care for a minor bite pending Qatar review
Content: Wash the area, avoid scratching, elevate it if comfortable, and use a cold pack wrapped in cloth for short periods; do not apply ice directly. Pain medicine, antihistamine, or topical steroid selection and dose require age, weight, pregnancy or breastfeeding status, allergies, comorbidities, sedation and interaction risk, skin integrity, and Qatar formulary approval. This UAT branch remains non-telemedicine pending governance.
Call Back If: swelling worsens; signs of infection or allergic reaction develop; facial swelling, breathing difficulty, dizziness, or rapid worsening.

references: NHS.UK, "Insect bites and stings", https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/insect-bites-and-stings/ (page last reviewed 01 June 2023)
